dialog.title: Elkan 5e

content.header: Hope you're enjoying the Elkan 5e module
content.headerText: See the Changelog button below for recent changes.
content.hint: This dialog will appear again when the module is updated.
content.updateNotice: If you were using our content before DND5e v4+ and have just updated to after V4+, you will find many of your previous characters, NPCs, and features may not be working properly. We recommend you re-create all player characters and replace features on NPCs as needed.
content.joinUsText:
Check out our website at Elkan5e.com.
For discussion, bug reporting, future polls, and news on upcoming content, join our Discord.
If you like our work, you can support us on Patreon or Ko-fi.

updateElkan.title: Elkan 5e Automatic Update Abilities
updateElkan.name: Update Items
updateElkan.label: Update Items
updateElkan.hint: Updates Elkan 5e features, items and spells on characters and NPCs to the current versions. Each row can also update from other installed modules instead. Preview first.
updateElkan.description: Brings characters and NPCs up to date with the Elkan 5e compendiums after a system or module update.

form.warningNote: Note: This Migration Tool is in beta and may cause bugs or interact with custom content in unexpected ways. We strongly recommend making a backup of your world before running it. If you have NPCs with tokens on the board—especially unlinked tokens—you may see duplicates of some abilities. If you encounter an issue, please report it on our Discord .

build.title: Ancestry, background and class
build.hint: If the new version asks for a choice that cannot be carried over, a list opens afterwards so you can make those choices yourself.
build.name: Update a Character's Ancestry, Background and Class
build.label: Update Character Build
build.menuHint: Pick one character and update its ancestry, background, class and subclass to the current Elkan 5e versions. Players can do this for their own characters. Anything that needs a new choice is offered to you afterwards.
build.intro: Updates one character's ancestry, background, class and subclass to the current Elkan 5e versions. Class levels, spent hit dice and the choices already made are kept.
build.confirmBody: This changes the selected character. Back up first if you are unsure. Choices that cannot be kept are offered to you afterwards.
build.choicesBody: These parts of the character have a choice that could not be carried over. Open each one and go to its Advancement tab to choose.
build.warning: Note: This tool is in beta. If you are unsure, ask your GM to back up the world first. Class levels, spent hit dice and the choices you already made are kept.

ui.intro: Updates keep each item where it is, so its sheet position, favorites, hotbar links and level-up tracking stay intact. Quantity, equipped, attunement, prepared state and spent uses are kept.
ui.duplicatesPlayers: Characters: remove spells and features that are exact copies
ui.duplicatesNpcs: NPCs: remove spells and features that are exact copies
ui.modulesHint: Tick the modules to use as sources. Where an item exists in both Elkan 5e and a module, Elkan 5e wins. Rows set to Elkan only join the same run.
ui.duplicatesHint: Only items that match another item on the same actor in every field are removed.
ui.nothing: Choose at least one thing to update.
ui.confirmBody: This changes items on your actors. Make sure you have a backup of your world. Use Preview changes first if you haven't.

modules.name: Update Items From Other Modules
modules.label: Update From Other Modules
modules.hint: Updates items, spells and features that came from other installed modules, using those modules' compendiums. Preview first.
modules.title: Update From Other Modules
modules.intro: Updates items, spells and features that came from the ticked modules, in place, keeping quantity, equipped, attunement, prepared state and spent uses. Elkan 5e content is not touched here.
modules.none: No active module has Item compendiums, so there is nothing to update from.
modules.pickOne: Tick at least one module first.

scrolls.name: Spell Scroll Rules
scrolls.hint: Characters need a class with spell slots to use spell scrolls. Spells on their list use their own attack bonus and save DC. Other spells need a check (DC 10 + spell level) and use +5 to hit and DC 13.
scrolls.notSpellcaster: {name} can't cast from a spell scroll. Only spellcasters with a class that gives spell slots can.
scrolls.checkPrompt: {spell} isn't on your spell list. Choose a skill for the DC {dc} check.
scrolls.checkFailed: {name} fails to cast {spell} from the scroll. The scroll isn't used up and can be tried again.
